List active task titles for the connected account, including pagination

guide.summary: Use Todoist OAuth with the read-only data:read scope for each customer's individual account. Request only data:read, then page through GET /api/v1/tasks with the cursor. Do not request data:read_write, data:delete or task:add. Provider review and customer-install approval policy are not in the supplied sources and remain unknowns.

findings.title: Todoist documents OAuth app authorization
findings.detail: Todoist documents an OAuth authorization URL with client_id, scope, state and response_type=code. Redirect the user to that URL to start consent.

evidence.quote: Easy setup: OAuth in a minute.
https://app.todoist.com/oauth/authorize?client_id = 0123456789abcdef & scope = data:read,data:delete & state = secretstring & response_type = code
Redirect users to the authorization URL at the endpoint

findings.title: Request data:read for listing active tasks
findings.detail: data:read grants read-only access to application data, including tasks. It is the narrowest documented grant that covers listing active tasks.

evidence.quote: data:read Grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.
Get Tasks Get all active tasks for the user.
get /api/v1/tasks https://api.todoist.com /api/v1/tasks

findings.title: Do not request write or delete scopes
findings.detail: data:read_write includes write access, and data:delete and task:add are outside this read-only use case. Do not request them, even though the registration example shows data:read_write.

evidence.quote: data:read_write Grants read and write access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters. This scope includes task:add and data:read scopes.
data:delete Grants permission to delete application data, including tasks, labels, and filters.
task:add Grants permission to add new tasks (the application cannot read or modify any existing data).
"redirect_uris": ["https://example.com/callback"], "scope": "data:read_write",

findings.title: Pagination uses next_cursor
findings.detail: Request the first page without a cursor, then pass next_cursor as cursor. Keep the same parameters on every page.

evidence.quote: To fetch the first page of results, make a request without a cursor parameter:
Subsequent Requests To fetch the next page, include the cursor parameter with the value from next_cursor :
Important : Always use the same parameters (filters, sorting, etc.) when using a cursor. Changing parameters between paginated requests may result in unexpected behavior or errors.
response as the cursor value for the next request.

steps.title: Register the Todoist OAuth app with a test redirect URI
steps.detail: Create the app in Todoist app management and set a test redirect URI. Record the client ID and secret outside source control.
steps.doneWhen: The app has a client ID and a registered redirect URI for the test environment.

evidence.quote: "redirect_uris": ["https://example.com/callback"], "scope": "data:read_write",
"grant_types": ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"], "response_types": ["code"],

steps.title: Implement the authorization redirect with scope data:read
steps.detail: Build the authorization URL with client_id, scope=data:read, a random state and response_type=code. Redirect the user to it and implement the callback that validates state.
steps.doneWhen: The generated authorization URL contains only scope=data:read and a state value.

evidence.quote: https://app.todoist.com/oauth/authorize?client_id = 0123456789abcdef & scope = data:read,data:delete & state = secretstring & response_type = code
Redirect users to the authorization URL at the endpoint
data:read Grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.

steps.title: Authorize a representative test Todoist account
steps.detail: Open the authorization URL with a test account, approve access and complete the callback. Confirm the granted access is data:read. Expected: a token response is received. Boundary check: confirm the consent screen shows read-only task access.
steps.doneWhen: The test account has granted data:read and the callback has received an authorization code.

evidence.quote: https://app.todoist.com/oauth/authorize?client_id = 0123456789abcdef & scope = data:read,data:delete & state = secretstring & response_type = code
Redirect users to the authorization URL at the endpoint
data:read Grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.

steps.title: Test listing active tasks with one page
steps.detail: Exchange the code for an OAuth access token, then request the first page. Replace YOUR_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN with the token from the token response. Expected: a 200 JSON response with results and next_cursor. Boundary check: confirm the request is GET only and no task changes occur.
steps.doneWhen: A 200 response returns active task results and next_cursor for the test account.

evidence.quote: curl "https://api.todoist.com/api/v1/tasks?limit=50" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"
Get Tasks Get all active tasks for the user.
get /api/v1/tasks https://api.todoist.com /api/v1/tasks

steps.title: Test cursor pagination for active tasks
steps.detail: Pass next_cursor from step 4 as cursor and keep limit=50. Repeat until next_cursor is null. Expected: each page returns task results and the final page has next_cursor null. Boundary check: confirm every page request is GET with the same filters.
steps.doneWhen: Pagination reaches a page with next_cursor null using only GET requests.

evidence.quote: Subsequent Requests To fetch the next page, include the cursor parameter with the value from next_cursor :
curl "https://api.todoist.com/api/v1/tasks?cursor=eyJwYWdlIjoyLCJsaW1pdCI6NTB9.aGFzaA&limit=50" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"
Important : Always use the same parameters (filters, sorting, etc.) when using a cursor. Changing parameters between paginated requests may result in unexpected behavior or errors.
response as the cursor value for the next request.

steps.title: Verify the read-only boundary
steps.detail: Inspect the granted scope and the outgoing request log for the test session. Expected: data:read only and only GET requests to /api/v1/tasks. Boundary check: confirm no POST, DELETE or write scope appears.
steps.doneWhen: The test log shows only GET requests and the granted scope is data:read.

evidence.quote: data:read Grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.
data:read_write Grants read and write access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters. This scope includes task:add and data:read scopes.

unknowns: Provider review requirements for publishing the app to other customer workspaces are not in the supplied sources. Verify with the Todoist developer program terms before launch.
Whether customer organization admins must approve installation is not documented in the supplied sources. Verify before rollout.
Whether the Todoist API documents a title field in the task response is not confirmed in the supplied excerpts. Verify the content field in the step 4 response.
The OAuth token expiry and refresh behavior is not fully confirmed in the supplied excerpts. Verify token lifetime during step 3.
